Subject: POC: Capacity planning & success criteria — ZenStack AI

Hi Aarav / Maya,

Thanks again for the call today — good alignment on goals. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the POC scheduled: 

POC scope & success criteria (as discussed)
- Primary success criteria: average response time (generation end-to-end) <= 500ms p95 for our 256-token prompt+completion profile during baseline load.
- Throughput target: support sustained 50 inference requests/sec across the POC dataset (peak target 150 req/sec for short bursts).
- Quality: automated evals on the seeded test set should match your current model baseline on L2 and semantic-similarity scores within a 5% delta.
- Stability: no more than 1% error/timeout rate over a 2-week observation window.

Capacity assumptions you shared:
- Typical sequence length ~200 tokens, 1 request = mean 300 tokens including context.
- Expected 500 active users during office hours, with periodic spikes up to ~1,500 concurrent users for <10 minutes.

Redwood recommended POC capacity (initial proposal)
- Reserved capacity: 2 x A100-40GB GPUs (baseline pool) to guarantee predictable latency and warm KV cache.
- Autoscaling policy: automatic scale-up to 6 GPU nodes during sustained high load (scale threshold: >60% GPU utilization for >60s).
- Burst/overflow behavior: short burst requests beyond autoscale cap will be routed to a quantized model variant with graceful degradation (lower cost, slightly higher latency) to protect SLAs.
- Cache/warmup plan: persistent prefix cache for common prompts; we recommend a 24-48 hour warmup window before the official evaluation window.

Operational & timeline
- Kickoff: week of Oct 19 — technical onboarding and dataset ingest (Marissa / Dylan to coordinate).
- Baseline run: Oct 26–Nov 2 (warmup + controlled traffic tests).
- Evaluation window: Nov 3–Nov 16 (2 weeks).
- Ownership: Redwood SE (Dylan Brooks) for infra/runbook; Redwood AE (Marissa Cole) for timelines and success gating; ZenStack PM (Aarav) for evaluation sign-off.

Next steps
1) Aarav — please confirm the success criteria above and the burst concurrency numbers so we can lock the reserved pool.
2) Dylan — can you draft the short capacity plan (node sizing, autoscale knobs, and fallback model plan) and attach to the thread?
3) I'll send a calendar invite for the kickoff and share the sample dataset upload instructions.

I've attached the draft POC requirements spreadsheet for your review (zenstack_poc_requirements.xlsx).

Thanks,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — this looks great and captures the discussion. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 50 req/sec sustained is correct for our baseline; the 150 req/sec peak is what we see in product tests. For the POC we can shape traffic to those numbers.
- For bursts, we prefer hard guarantees on baseline latency over trying to serve 100% of bursts. Can Redwood guarantee p95 <= 500ms for the baseline reserved pool (2 x A100) before we decide on autoscale caps? If not, let us know the recommended minimum reserved configuration.
- We have a procurement constraint: purchasing committed reserved capacity requires a short PO. Can you confirm expected cost delta between 2 x A100 baseline vs 4 x A100 (rough order of magnitude) so we can route internally?

Also: attaching our short POC checklist (I pulled a few items into the sheet you sent).

Hi Aarav — quick technical note on capacity and guarantees. Apologies for the long email but wanted to be explicit so procurement has what they need.

Guaranteed baseline (recommended)
- Config: 2 x A100-40GB reserved nodes (persistent pool).
- Expected perf: for your prompt profile (mean 300 tokens) we estimate ~45–55 req/sec steady-state at p95 <= 500ms when using optimized kernels and persistent KV cache. That aligns with your 50 req/sec baseline but leaves minimal headroom.

If you want a tighter latency buffer (comfort for spikes) we recommend 4 x A100-40GB reserved which increases baseline capacity to ~120 req/sec at similar latency targets (p95 <= 500ms) and reduces autoscale pressure.

Autoscale & burst behavior
- Autoscale policy: scale when avg GPU util > 60% for 60s; cool down 120s. Scale steps: +1 GPU node (up to max) per interval.
- Autoscale cap: propose max 6 reserved-compatible nodes for the POC (so baseline 2 -> burst to 6). That should cover your 150 req/sec short bursts when combined with short-queueing windows.
- Overflow: when autoscale is saturated, traffic will be routed to our quantized-variant endpoints (approx 2–3x cost reduction) with slightly higher latency (~700–900ms p95) but preserves throughput and prevents errors.

Warmup & cache
- Persistent KV cache will require a warmup period; suggest pre-warming 24–48 hours before evaluation window. We can coordinate a synthetic traffic run to pre-fill the cache.

Estimated cost delta (very rough order)
- 2 x A100 reserved baseline: estimated incremental committed POC cost = $18k–$25k / month (depends on term/concessions).
- 4 x A100 reserved baseline: estimated incremental cost = $35k–$45k / month.
- Autoscale is billed for actual peak node-minutes; short bursts are economical if they remain brief (<15m).

Attachments: I exported a short capacity plan with the above numbers (redwood_poc_capacity_plan.pdf).

If that looks good I can finalize the autoscale policy and we can include the sizing notes in the SOW/PO.

Cheers,
Dylan Brooks
